README: Validate_commands provides, module & method name as
<module name>.<method name>
NOTE: module name could have '.'
The last element separated by  '.' is considered as
method name
e.g. 'show.acl.test_acl'
Here we load 'show.acl' and call 'test_acl' method on it.
called as:
<module>.<method>>(<config before change>,
<config after change>, <affected keys>)
config is in JSON format as in config_db.json
affected_keys in same format, but w/o value
{ 'ACL_TABLE': { 'SNMP_ACL': {} ... }, ...}
The affected keys has 'added', 'updated' & 'deleted'
Multiple validate commands may be provided.
Note: The commands may be called in any order
A table may also list 'restart_on_change' rules, each as
{ 'units': [ <systemd unit>, ... ], 'fields': [ <field>, ... ],
'modified_only': true, 'reset_failed': [ <unit>, ... ],
'host_only': true }
Only 'units' is required. Rules are matched against each change
of a patch as it is applied. After the last change (or after one
fails), each unit of a matched rule is restarted once, after
'systemctl reset-failed' of the unit and of the 'reset_failed' units.
Without 'fields' any difference in the table matches. With it,
the rule matches when one of those fields differs in some key of
the table; a missing, empty-string or empty-list value counts as
unset. With 'modified_only', a field only counts when it is set
both before and after.
Rules apply in every scope whose patch changes the table, unless
'host_only' limits them to the host scope. A unit whose FEATURE
state is disabled or always_disabled is skipped.
